title: Water Leak Inspection Checklist Form
subtitle: An original water leak workflow that guides a bounded inspection from readiness through findings and release, with explicit qualified-review, stop-work, escalation, and accountable handoff controls.
description: A workflow-complete water leak inspection checklist form for the suspected or confirmed water-release location that captures exact identity, domain observations, supporting evidence, decisions, exceptions, responsible owners, and closeout without replacing professional judgment or the organization's controlling procedures.
use_case: Use when an assigned inspector must confirm safe observation boundaries, document domain-specific conditions, route deficiencies, and record a qualified acceptance, restriction, or follow-up decision. The leak response coordinator owns routing, and closure requires documented evidence, disposition of restrictions, and acceptance by the designated reviewer.

sections.title: Water leak inspection identity and authority
sections.guidance: Define the asset, inspection scope, qualified reviewer, and conditions before observations begin.

sections.title: Water leak readiness and safe observation boundary
sections.guidance: Confirm identity, operating context, access, and limits before checking condition.

blocks.label: Stop-work boundary
blocks.guidance: Do not enter water near electrical equipment, stand below a sagging ceiling, or handle suspected contaminated water. Keep occupants clear and use the organization's emergency route for rapid flooding, structural movement, gas odor, or critical-service impact. Only authorized personnel may operate shutoffs after evaluating downstream consequences.

sections.title: Water leak inspection points and finding evidence
sections.guidance: Check each point only when observed; use the findings table for condition, evidence, and disposition.

blocks.label: Domain inspection checklist
items: Location, reporter, first-observed time, and active-flow status are confirmed
Electrical equipment, ceiling sag, contamination, slip, and structural conditions are screened first
Water source remains described as suspected until supported by isolation or repair evidence
Visible fixture, pipe, valve, roof, drain, appliance, and equipment conditions are documented
Meter, submeter, flow indicator, or pressure evidence is captured by approved method
Affected rooms, finishes, contents, equipment, and adjacent spaces are mapped
Known water type, odor, color, temperature, and contamination uncertainty are recorded
Shutoff ownership and consequences for occupants, processes, and fire protection are checked
Temporary containment, public protection, and access restrictions are documented
Repair, utility, drying, environmental, electrical, and restoration referrals are assigned
Post-isolation and post-repair verification readings are time-stamped
Recurring moisture, hidden damage, and unresolved limitations have owners

fields.label: Inaccessible areas, sampling limits, representative conditions, trends, and supporting context

sections.title: Water leak exceptions, stop conditions, and escalation
sections.guidance: Make every unresolved condition visible with an immediate control, owner, due point, and final disposition.

blocks.label: Stop-condition screen
items: Water contacting electrical equipment, outlets, panels, cords, or machinery
Bulging or sagging ceiling, unstable finish, structural movement, or falling material
Suspected sewage, chemical, fire-water, or other contaminated release
Rapid flooding, washout, sinkhole, severe pressure, or uncontrolled flow
Slip exposure, hidden opening, poor visibility, or unsafe access
Shutoff would impair fire protection, medical, process, or critical service
Gas odor, steam, hot water, refrigerant, or unknown fluid is also present
Condition exceeds responder authority, equipment, training, or protective controls
blocks.guidance: Check any condition observed or reported; checking an item does not mean the condition is controlled.

blocks.label: Qualified-person and stop-work boundary
blocks.guidance: Do not enter water near electrical equipment, stand below a sagging ceiling, or handle suspected contaminated water. Keep occupants clear and use the organization's emergency route for rapid flooding, structural movement, gas odor, or critical-service impact. Only authorized personnel may operate shutoffs after evaluating downstream consequences.

blocks.label: Exception and escalation register
blocks.guidance: Link each inspection exception to supporting evidence and keep it open until disposition is recorded.

sections.title: Water leak decision, handoff, and accountable closeout
sections.guidance: Record the decision, remaining limitations, next action, and the people accountable for acceptance.

blocks.label: Closeout completeness
items: Suspected or confirmed water-release location identity and location were reconciled
Observed facts, measurements, and evidence references are complete
Decision authority and applicable review requirements were confirmed
Stop conditions, restrictions, and open exceptions remain visible
Customer, operations, or site handoff was recorded
Next action, owner, due point, and record-retention route are explicit

fields.label: Limitations, assumptions, restrictions, customer message, and next-action context

blocks.label: Accountable review and handoff
blocks.guidance: Signatures acknowledge the recorded decision and handoff; they do not waive unresolved restrictions.
